simple.meaning: מְלוּכָה (mᵉlûwkâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “something ruled , i.e. a realm.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Samuel 10:16. The surrounding context includes kingship, city, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מְלוּכָה (H4410) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

timeline.evidenceText: Saul said to his uncle, “He told us plainly that the donkeys were found.” But concerning the matter of the kingdom, of which Samuel spoke, he didn’t tell him.
Then Samuel told the people the regulations of the kingdom, and wrote it in a book, and laid it up before Yahweh. Samuel sent all the people away, every man to his house.
Then Samuel said to the people, “Come! Let’s go to Gilgal, and renew the kingdom there.”

Now when Saul had taken the kingdom over Israel, he fought against all his enemies on every side, against Moab, and against the children of Ammon, and against Edom, and against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines. Wherever he turned himself, he defeated them.
Saul was very angry, and this saying displeased him. He said, “They have creditd David with ten thousands, and they have only credited me with thousands. What can he have more but the kingdom?”
Now Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.

Yahweh has returned on you all the blood of Saul’s house, in whose place you have reigned! Yahweh has delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son! Behold, you are caught by your own mischief, because you are a man of blood!”
Also, Solomon sits on the throne of the kingdom.

He said, “You know that the kingdom was mine, and that all Israel set their faces on me, that I should reign. However the kingdom is turned around, and has become my brother’s; for it was his from Yahweh.

He said, “You know that the kingdom was mine, and that all Israel set their faces on me, that I should reign. However the kingdom is turned around, and has become my brother’s; for it was his from Yahweh.

King Solomon answered his mother, “Why do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask for him the kingdom also; for he is my elder brother; even for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab the son of Zeruiah.”
but I will take the kingdom out of his son’s hand, and will give it to you, even ten tribes.

When Rehoboam had come to Jerusalem, he assembled all the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen men, who were warriors, to fight against the house of Israel, to bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam the son of Solomon.
Jezebel his wife said to him, “Do you now govern the kingdom of Israel? Arise, and eat bread, and let your heart be merry. I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.”

But in the seventh month, Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the royal offspring came, and ten men with him, and struck Gedaliah, so that he died, with the Jews and the Chaldeans that were with him at Mizpah.
and didn’t inquire of Yahweh. Therefore he killed him, and turned the kingdom over to David the son of Jesse.
All the rich ones of the earth shall eat and worship.
They shall call its nobles to the kingdom, but none shall be there;
You will also be a crown of beauty in Yahweh‘s hand,

Now in the seventh month, Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the royal offspring and one of the chief officers of the king, and ten men with him, came to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to Mizpah; and there they ate bread together in Mizpah.

definitions.full: H4410. melukah מְלוּכָה noun feminine kingship, royalty ; — ׳מ absolute 1Sam 10:16 23 t.; — kingship, kingly office, royalty: 10:16 , 25 ; 11:14 ; 18:5 ; 1Kin 2:15 (twice in verse); 2:22 ; 11:35 ; 1Chr 10:14 ; Isa 34:12 ; belonging to ׳י Obadiah 21; Psa 22:29 (|| בַּגּוֺיִם וּמשֵׁל ); מ ׳לָכַד עַל 1Sam 14:47 assume sovereignty over ; מ ׳נָתַן בְּיַד 2Sam 16:18 give kingship to (subject ׳י ); מ ׳הֵשִׁיב ׳ל 1Kin 12:21 restore kingship to ; מ ׳עָשָׂה על 21:7 exercise kingship over ; metaphor of Jerusalem לִמְלוּכָה וַתִּצְלְחִי Ezek 16:13 (strike out ᵐ5 Co); הַמ ׳עִיר 2Sam 12:26 = royal city ; compare הַמ ׳כִּסֵּא 1Kin 1:46 ; הַמ ׳זֶרַע 2Kin 25:25 so Jer 41:1 ; Ezek 17:13 ; Dan 1:3 ; מ ׳צְנִו֯ף Isa 62:3 (|| תִּפְאֶרֶת עֲטֶרֶת ).
